# Game design brief

## Player fantasy

What does the player get to feel capable of doing? Which audience is this for, and which Roblox devices are first-class targets?

## Core loop

Describe one complete session as actions, feedback, outcomes, and the reason to repeat. Keep deterministic rules separate from presentation.

## State and authority

List state owned by server, client presentation, persistence, remotes, and validation rules. Treat client requests as untrusted.

## Progression and social play

Describe short, medium, and long-term progression; co-op/competition roles; recovery after disconnect; and replay variation that changes decisions rather than only appearance.

## Art and audio direction

Define silhouettes, material language, lighting, color, camera, animation, effects, sound, readability, asset budget, and provenance requirements.

## Monetization and privacy

State whether monetization is out of scope or describe a transparent optional design. Identify data events, retention, age appropriateness, and policy review.

## Success measures and hypotheses

Separate measurable product questions from evidence. Do not invent retention, conversion, or market validation.

## Acceptance and playtest plan

Write actual player tasks, edge cases, accessibility checks, target device checks, performance budgets, and expected console/screenshot evidence.
